user.title: Strømkalkulator
user.description:
Complete overview of electricity costs: grid tariffs, government subsidies, and Norgespris comparison.

Select your grid company to get started. Tax zone is set automatically.

data_description.boligtype: Residence: Subsidy up to 5000 kWh/month, Norgespris up to 5000 kWh/month. Holiday home: No subsidy, Norgespris up to 1000 kWh/month. Holiday home (permanent residence): Same as residence (Regulation § 11).
data_description.har_norgespris: Enable if you have ordered Norgespris at Elhub (minside.elhub.no), not from your grid company or electricity provider. Fixed price (50 øre/kWh in southern Norway, 40 øre in northern Norway) for the first 5000 kWh per month (1000 kWh for holiday homes). Consumption above the limit is billed at spot price.

sensors.title: Select sensors
sensors.description: Select the sensors the integration should use for calculating grid tariffs and subsidies.

data.spotpris_inkl_mva: Spot price sensor delivers prices incl. VAT

data_description.power_sensor: Sensor showing current power consumption in watts, e.g. from HAN port, Tibber Pulse, or P1 meter.
data_description.spot_price_sensor: Sensor with current spot price in NOK/kWh. Usually 'Current price' from the Nord Pool integration.
data_description.spotpris_inkl_mva: Leave off for HA-core nordpool integration (delivers excl. VAT). Turn on if your sensor already includes VAT (e.g. the older custom_components/nordpool with VAT=true, or a custom template sensor).
data_description.energy_sensor: Cumulative kWh counter from the AMS smart meter. Recommended for exact invoice numbers. See docs/input-sensorer.md for details.
data_description.electricity_provider_price_sensor: Sensor with the total price from your electricity provider (e.g. Tibber 'Electricity price'). Only used to populate the 'Total price (electricity contract)' sensor for comparison against your actual contract. Does not affect any other calculation. Skip if you have spot price directly or Norgespris.
data_description.export_power_sensor: Power sensor for export to the grid (OBIS 2.7.0) in watts, for prosumers with solar panels only. Used to calculate export revenue and net monthly cost. Skip if you don't have solar panels.

sikring.title: Main fuse size
sikring.description: {dso} charges the fixed grid fee by the size of your main fuse (overcurrent protection), not by the power you draw. Pick the row printed on your grid invoice or in your fuse box. If in doubt, ask {dso}. This cannot be read from the meter.

data_description.sikringstrinn: The rows are quoted verbatim from the grid company price list. Note that the rate can depend on system voltage (230 V or 400 V).

pricing.title: Custom pricing
pricing.description: Select your tax zone and enter energy tariff prices in NOK/kWh excl. VAT and excl. consumption tax/Enova fee. The integration adds taxes and VAT based on tax zone. We have no price list for the capacity fee (the fixed part), so you need to take it from your own.

data.energiledd_dag: Energy tariff day (NOK/kWh, excl. VAT and taxes)
data.energiledd_natt: Energy tariff night/weekend (NOK/kWh, excl. VAT and taxes)
data.egendefinert_kapasitetstrinn: Capacity tiers from your price list (optional)

data_description.avgiftssone: Determines VAT and consumption tax. The VAT exemption follows county, not price area: 'Nord-Norge' covers Nordland and Troms, 'Tiltakssonen' covers Finnmark and Nord-Troms (VAT Act § 6-6). Everyone else, including NO3 (Trøndelag and Møre og Romsdal), selects 'Sør-Norge' and pays 25% VAT.
data_description.energiledd_dag: Grid tariff only, for daytime. Find the amount listed as 'energiledd' or 'overføring' on your price list, before consumption tax, Enova fee and VAT.
data_description.energiledd_natt: Grid tariff only, for night/weekend. If your grid company uses a flat rate, enter the same value as for daytime.
data_description.egendefinert_kapasitetstrinn: The fixed grid fee as your grid company lists it: kW limit and NOK/month incl. VAT, separated by a colon, with tiers separated by commas. The notation 2:155,5:250,10:415 means NOK 155/month up to 2 kW, NOK 250/month from 2 to 5 kW and NOK 415/month above 5 kW; the numbers are a format example, not prices. The top tier covers everything above the limit below it. Leave the field empty and capacity tier, monthly grid rent, monthly total, estimated monthly cost and accumulated cost stay unknown. That is deliberate: there is no price list behind 'Custom', and a guessed fixed fee looks like a price without being one.

reconfigure.title: Strømkalkulator settings
reconfigure.description:
Change grid company, sensors or Norgespris settings.

The energiledd fields are overrides. Leave them empty and the grid company's price list applies, with the rate updating itself whenever the list changes. The price list for {dso} currently states day {katalog_dag} and night {katalog_natt}, in øre/kWh with taxes and VAT. A custom grid company has no price list, so there the numbers you entered yourself always apply.

error.already_configured: This power sensor is already used by another Strømkalkulator instance
error.spot_unit_invalid: The sensor does not have a price unit the calculator can convert. NOK/kWh, kr/kWh, øre/kWh and NOK/MWh all work and are converted automatically. EUR does not, since we have no exchange rate.
error.spot_value_unreasonable: The value is too high to be an electricity price. Converted to NOK/kWh it exceeds 100 kroner, so you have probably picked a total cost in kroner instead of a price.
error.enhet_ukjent: The calculator does not recognise the unit this sensor reports, so it cannot convert the value. Power must be W, kW or MW. Energy must be Wh, kWh or MWh. Price must be NOK/kWh, kr/kWh, øre/kWh or NOK/MWh.
error.enhet_feil_dimensjon: The sensor measures something other than what the field asks for. Check that the power field points at a power sensor, the energy field at a cumulative kWh meter, and the price fields at a price per kWh.
error.enhet_feil_valuta: The price is in a currency other than kroner. The calculator has no exchange rate, so a EUR sensor cannot be used directly. Pick a sensor in NOK/kWh or øre/kWh, or build a template sensor that converts.
error.energi_ikke_kumulativ: The energy sensor must be a counter that only increases, that is state_class total_increasing or total. We measure the difference between readings, and a sensor showing present consumption has no difference to measure.
error.trinntabell_ugyldig: The capacity tiers could not be read. Write each tier as kW limit and NOK/month separated by a colon, tiers separated by commas, with increasing kW limits: 2:155,5:250,10:415.

vakthold_utfall.title: Strømkalkulator is not receiving data from {input}
vakthold_utfall.description: {entity_id} has been unavailable for {timer} hours. While it is gone, consumption and cost stand still without the numbers looking wrong. Check the integration that owns the sensor, the HAN reader and the network. The warning clears itself once data returns.

vakthold_frossen.title: The energy meter is not moving
vakthold_frossen.description: {entity_id} has not increased for {timer} hours. The sensor still reports, but the counter is stuck, so monthly consumption comes out too low. If the site really has no consumption, raise the threshold in settings. The warning clears itself once the counter increases again.

vakthold_spot_utlopt.title: The spot price is too old to calculate with
vakthold_spot_utlopt.description: {entity_id} has not delivered a valid price for {timer} hours, and the cached price has expired. Consumption is still counted in kWh, but cost, subsidy and the Norgespris comparison stand still until the price returns.

energi_delta_forkastet.title: A jump in the energy meter was discarded

confirm.title: A jump in the energy meter was discarded
confirm.description: {sensor} jumped {kwh} kWh since the previous reading on {forrige}. The jump was kept out of monthly consumption, since it could just as well be a meter swap or a sensor glitch as real usage. If it was real, those kWh are now missing from the monthly figure and the invoice will exceed the estimate. Confirm to close the warning.

satser_utdatert.title: Grid tariff and tax rates may be outdated
satser_utdatert.description: The rates in Strømkalkulator are verified for {aar}. The calendar has rolled over and the integration is still using {aar} rates. Check HACS for an updated version, otherwise grid tariffs, taxes and subsidy may be wrong for the current year.

norgespris_utlopt.title: The Norgespris scheme may have ended
norgespris_utlopt.description: The Norgespris scheme was decided through {aar}. You have Norgespris enabled, but the scheme may have ended or changed terms. Check the current rules and turn off Norgespris in settings if it no longer applies to you.

confirm.title: Your grid company has merged
confirm.description: {old_name} is now part of {new_name}. The integration has been updated automatically, and consumption data and history are preserved.

sikringstrinn_mangler.title: Main fuse size missing
sikringstrinn_mangler.description: {dso} charges the fixed grid fee by your main fuse size, which cannot be read from the meter. Until you pick it, the capacity tier sensor stays unknown and the fixed fee is missing from monthly cost and invoice estimates. Open Settings > Devices & Services > Strømkalkulator > Configure and pick the row printed on your grid invoice.

spotpris_mva_check.title: Spot price handling updated
spotpris_mva_check.description:
Strømkalkulator now treats the spot price sensor as excluding VAT (correct for the HA-core Nord Pool integration). The code previously assumed including VAT, and that gave 25 % errors in electricity subsidy and total price in Southern Norway. Most users don't need to do anything.

You only need to act if your spot price sensor already delivers prices including VAT. That applies if you have a custom template sensor that adds 25 %, or use the older custom_components/nordpool with VAT=true. In that case: open Strømkalkulator settings (Settings > Devices & Services > Strømkalkulator > Configure) and turn on 'Spot price sensor delivers prices including VAT'.

dso_delt.title: Your grid company is split into several price areas
dso_delt.description: {dso} has several price areas with different rates, and your address decides which one applies. We cannot pick for you. Open the Strømkalkulator settings and select the right area from: {omrader}. Until you do, the integration uses the middle area, so your grid tariff may be wrong.

egendefinert_energiledd.title: Check the energy tariff rate you entered

confirm.title: Check the energy tariff rate you entered
confirm.description:
Your grid company isn't in the list, so you entered the energy tariff rate yourself. Up to and including version 1.16.0 the field was labelled 'incl. taxes', while the integration treats the rate as grid tariff only and adds consumption tax, the Enova fee and VAT itself. If you followed that text, the taxes are counted twice, and the rate is about {avgifter} øre/kWh too high before VAT.

We can't see what you typed, only that the text was misleading. You currently have {dag} øre/kWh for daytime and {natt} øre/kWh for night and weekend. Compare with the line listed as 'energiledd' or 'overføring' on your grid company's price list, the one before taxes and VAT. If it needs correcting, do it in Settings > Devices & Services > Strømkalkulator > Configure. Confirm here once the rate is checked, and the warning is gone for good.

vakthold_enhet.title: Strømkalkulator cannot compute from {input}
vakthold_enhet.description: {entity_id} now reports in the unit {enhet}, which the calculator cannot convert. While the sensor stays that way it delivers no numbers, and everything that depends on it stands still. Check the integration that owns the sensor, or pick another one under Settings > Devices and services > Strømkalkulator > Configure.

prisenhet_ubekreftet.title: Confirm the unit on the price sensor

confirm.title: Confirm the unit on the price sensor
confirm.description:
{entity_id} reports no unit, and the calculator assumes the price is in NOK/kWh. This applies to {roller}. If that is correct, just confirm here and the notice is gone.

If the sensor is in øre/kWh or NOK/MWh, the numbers are off by a factor of a hundred and a thousand respectively. Set the right unit on the sensor, or pick another sensor, before confirming.

init.title: Choose which energiledd rate applies
init.description:
Your installation has an energiledd rate stored from an earlier setup: {lagret_dag} øre/kWh for day and {lagret_natt} øre/kWh for night and weekend, taxes and VAT included. The price list for {dso} currently states {katalog_dag} and {katalog_natt} øre/kWh.

Up to and including 1.16.0 the stored rate won over the price list, so a tariff change never reached you. That is fixed, and the installation uses the price list from now on. We simply do not know whether the stored number was your own choice, because setup stored the price list rate for everyone. Hence the question.

Choose to follow the price list and the stored number is removed, with the rate updating itself from then on. Choose to keep your own rates and {lagret_dag} and {lagret_natt} øre/kWh apply until you change them yourself in the settings.

egendefinert_fastledd.title: Capacity tiers missing for custom grid company
egendefinert_fastledd.description: Up to and including 1.16.0, 'Custom' shipped ten built-in capacity tiers. They were a template with no price list behind them, and since the capacity fee is a fixed monthly amount they fed straight into the monthly cost. They have been removed. Until you enter your own, 'Capacity tier', 'Monthly grid rent', 'Monthly total', 'Estimated monthly cost' and 'Accumulated cost' stay unknown, and the per-kWh prices are calculated without the fixed fee. Open Settings > Devices & Services > Strømkalkulator > Configure and enter the tiers from your price list as kW limit:NOK per month, separated by commas.
